approaches.name: Exact same-domain normalization before fillet selection
approaches.fitForWonky: Use a logical quotient of connected faces/edges on proven identical carriers before stripe generation. Keep geometric sameness, topology adjacency, orientation and source history distinct. For cylinders, prove parallel axes, zero perpendicular axis separation and equal radius; ignore parameter seam/frame differences, but preserve required periodic seam uses. Start with source-carrier identity, then exact predicates on stored input words. A fragment-only degree-two continuation belongs to one geometric edge regardless of tangentPropagation; propagation across a genuine G1 carrier change remains opt-in. OCCT's separate UnifyFaces/UnifyEdges/ConcatBSplines/KeepShape/History concepts support this separation.
approaches.risks: Do not copy OCCT's tolerance-based coincidence or enable spline concatenation to hide near-coincident features. Cone angle/frame equality needs provenance or a proved implicit-coefficient comparison, not an epsilon on angle. Merging must rebuild compatible 3D curves and pcurves without removing holes or shell boundaries. OCCT issue #1541 reports a 180-degree circle/pcurve phase mismatch and exploding tolerance after unification; it is a single unconfirmed report, useful as an adversary rather than proof that every version is broken.

approaches.name: Exact local event geometry instead of a generic vertex patch
approaches.fitForWonky: Extend HS-1 with one finite stripe-domain object: support region, edge sector/slab and both endpoint cut planes. Bounds first discover candidate obstacles; the corner stage clips them to the constructed domain before a final verdict. This handles KS07, short risers and cut-corner false overlaps with unchanged elementary surfaces. Distinguish no collision, tangent/consumed face, stripe consumption, selected-neighbour meet and unsupported overflow as separate topology events. The final clearance check must include face-region occupancy, including a face covering a cap without any edge crossing it.
approaches.risks: Ignoring an obstacle because one limiting point is beyond a mitre is insufficient: another portion may enter the clipped stripe. Removing the enclosing-ball test without a replacement is unsafe. Broad-phase boxes, edge samples and positive Jacobians alone are not global collision proofs. Preserve a named refusal when trimmed-face occupancy cannot be decided.

approaches.name: Finite-candidate ellipse-arc and algebraic trim predicates
approaches.fitForWonky: New derivation: for the existing RL axial metric, substitute X(t)=c+u*cos(t)+v*sin(t), obtaining lambda(t)=C+A*cos(t)+B*sin(t). The minimum on a clipped arc is among its endpoints, stationary directions plus/minus(A,B)/sqrt(A^2+B^2), and intersections with domain cut planes. Use oriented arc membership and exact/radical comparisons without deciding from approximate atan2. For a radial-plane distance metric, differentiating squared projected distance gives a trigonometric polynomial of degree two, reducible to a quartic by tan(t/2); isolate all roots or refuse. Keep exact conic/algebraic trims in the model and certify only representations that really need approximation.
approaches.risks: The simple sinusoid formula does not cover every TC/RP/RL metric. The rational half-angle chart needs its omitted t=pi endpoint, branch ordering and multiple-root handling. Stored ellipse points and frames can contain construction error; predicate exactness on stored words must not be inflated into exactness of their intended construction. Example z=.4+.2*cos(t), t in [-pi/3,pi/3], has minimum .5 versus whole-ellipse .2: a .42 chamfer can be admitted, but only after the complete support/end-domain check.

approaches.name: Analytic sphere/torus corner ladder; cyclides only for the right semantics
approaches.fitForWonky: Keep existing equal-radius trihedral spheres. Admit higher-valence plane corners only if a common offset-plane centre exists, all contact domains fit, and the spherical patch is manifold. FP14 remains the much cheaper exact toroidal roll with major radius r_concave+r_convex, not a Gregory problem. Dupin cyclides give exact rational biquadratic transitions for special compatible configurations; Wallner-Pottmann gives designer-controlled exact rational C1 transitions between quadrics. These are useful future transition features, not a substitute for the prescribed constant-radius edge stripes.
approaches.risks: Three independent offset planes give a candidate sphere, not guaranteed valid trims; four or more planes are generally inconsistent. A generic Dupin cyclide has variable rolling-sphere radius, and general constant-radius pipes are not necessarily rational. Rationality of a surface does not certify trimming, clearance or Parasolid equivalence. Avoid adding a Cyclide type for current R20 without a concrete case needing it.

approaches.name: Boundary-first Gregory or Hahn n-sided fill, with explicit shape policy
approaches.fitForWonky: Build on the existing Varady-Rockwood/Vida-Martin-Varady notes, not an invented rereading of their inaccessible full texts. A general setback boundary alternates stripe cross-curves and support spring-curves, up to 2n sides. New primary reading: Hettinga-Kosinka 2018 resolves incompatible corner twists with rational Gregory terms; its Gregory-GB representation has 5n+1 controls instead of the much larger S-patch net. SISL s1391 first prepares cross-boundary derivative curves, then sh1460 uses Hahn's split into n quadrilateral Coons patches of orders 7 and 5. This is a practical alternative to one monolithic n-sided surface, but not a turnkey fillet operator.
approaches.risks: G1 boundary interpolation does not establish injectivity, global nonintersection, prescribed radius or a unique design. The 2018 paper explicitly reports foldovers for some nonconvex polygons and has removable corner parametrization singularities. Its mesh/normal-based construction must not replace exact CAD boundary curves. Zhou-Qian 2010 advertises an exact rational S-patch polyhedral setback construction, but only its metadata/search abstract was accessible; do not promise its scope or numerical certification. 'Suitcase corner' is ambiguous CAD vocabulary, not a unique geometric specification.

approaches.name: Permissive patch evaluator as a mathematical reference, not production fallback
approaches.fitForWonky: The earlier chapter already lists salvipeter/transfinite; this pass read commit 2324dcb781844e98aca686441e156b820a993baa. Its MIT corner-based evaluator blends ribbon interpolants. Surface::overrideNormalFence can supply true support normals; the default ribbon normal is a rotation-minimizing frame and is not automatically the CAD support normal. Reimplement analytic boundary jets and removable-limit evaluation in Bend. Use a rational/Bezier subdivision certificate for positive denominators, boundary-position and normal error, regularity, and patch/body separation; the certificate must gate emitted geometry, not exist only as a report.
approaches.risks: Direct port is not certified: surface.cc:267-282 estimates twists with step 1e-4; :187-218 and :300-303 have epsilon/zero branches. parameterization-barycentric.cc:23-35 documents a workaround that is discontinuous outside its stated domain. OCCT CnCrn is no stronger: :2697-2706 warns G1 constraints can undulate; :3488-3495 samples the contour and uses max(tolapp,10*G0Error). SISL/OCCT are study/oracle sources, not production dependencies. An exact rational patch is exact for its chosen definition, not automatically the same shape as an Onshape setback.

approaches.name: Commercial compatibility is a separate contract from mathematical validity
approaches.fitForWonky: Rechecked primary docs: Onshape opFillet defaults tangentPropagation=false, allowEdgeOverflow=true, smoothCorners=false; UI tangent propagation is enabled by default. Parasolid's published older contract distinguishes unspecified setback from zero: unspecified lets the kernel choose, zero prevents setback on that edge; user setbacks require all edges at a valence>=3 vertex and do not apply to chamfers. ACIS distinguishes minimum/no-setback, autosetback and autoblend; autosetback forces n-sided patches, while autoblend can retain simple spheres/tori. Preserve these distinctions rather than treating every vertex-blend refusal as permission to insert any smooth patch.
approaches.risks: The public Parasolid manual is old and does not specify today's Onshape sizing heuristics. Onshape's optional Smooth fillet corners is not evidence that default opFillet disables every automatic setback. Archived surface points constrain shape but cannot prove an unknown default rule. KS01's two inferred offset ranges are not enough to derive the conversion from width=.42 or selection-order invariance. Patents and source licenses require review before copying algorithms; private use is not a blanket patent exemption.

recommendation: Keep the analytic/local-surgery architecture. Execute the existing house-style plan with the new exact-domain and carrier-identity details below, rather than starting a general fillet rewrite. First FVB-01 and FVB-03, then FVB-05/FVB-06 and FVB-07; take FVB-04 beside the bounds work, FVB-02 when split curved carriers reach R20, and FVB-08 for KS04. FVB-09 is a small optional exact extension. General setback filling FVB-10 and KS01 FVB-11 remain opt-in and gated by a defined shape policy and necessary curve infrastructure. All production geometry remains Bend. Shared acceptance: freeze minimal R20 inputs with provenance; assert meaningful changed geometry, topology, analytic carrier/radius and G1 conditions; independently validate exported STEP with OCCT through uv; compare closed forms or certified integration bounds plus archived Onshape geometry where available; run planted negatives and js/cpu1, then cpuN at integration. Do not count a new refusal as completed capability, a sample maximum as a certificate, or agreement with Onshape's approximate mean volume as exactness. Existing house-style quadrature convergence to 1e-12 is evidence, not by itself a rigorous integration bound. Estimates assume 8 hours per agent-day, informed by 1-3-hour local fixes and the 8-hour five-cause hybrid fix; local packages include verification, new freeform infrastructure has roughly factor-two uncertainty. The nine exact/local packages total 7.25 agent-days; optional bounded freeform and KS01 work add 7, excluding external SSI prerequisites and any wait for authorized reference probes. This is planning, not a claim these capabilities were implemented.

packages.title: FVB-10: Opt-in certified setback patch for a bounded polyhedral family
packages.scope: After the analytic packages, implement a narrow experimental corner family, initially three blended edges with unequal radii and explicit setbacks on planar supports. Construct the alternating cross/spring boundary and support-normal ribbons, then a Gregory or Hahn-style fill in Bend with analytic derivatives and corner limits. Introduce a production patch representation and bounded STEP/mesh export. Admission must prove boundary closure/G1 budget, denominator bounds, local regularity plus a sufficient global embedding/separation condition; difficult domains return vertex-patch-uncertified. Keep exact rational construction separate from certified approximation of that target, and both separate from Parasolid shape parity.
packages.acceptance: Minimal 30-mm box corner with radii 1/2/3 mm and explicit 6-mm setbacks must produce a nonempty closed opt-in model and STEP, with an explicit proposed export budget of 0.001 mm and boundary-normal budget of 1e-4 rad. An independently written high-precision/rational evaluator checks boundary jets and certificate subdivision leaves; OCCT via uv checks imported topology and edge/surface consistency. Also retain an equal-radius spherical control and a deliberately twisted/nonconvex boundary that cannot certify. Planted negatives: swap ribbon order, use the default RMF normal instead of a support normal, insert a narrow interior fold between samples, and underreport export error. All must be detected. Matching a frozen Onshape corner is a separate prerequisite for exposing this as default-compatible opFillet.
packages.r20Impact: Future general vertex-blend capability; no current evidence it unlocks more R20 than the exact packages. Estimate covers only the bounded family, patch representation and certification/export path, not arbitrary n, general curved supports or general spline Booleans.

openQuestions: Which house-style packages have landed in other active worktrees since this snapshot? Reconcile by code and frozen case outputs before scheduling; this report did not run the fillet suites or live R20.

FP17/FP18/FP19/FP21/FP22 are proposed references in <repo>/docs/fillet-housestyle.md:741-754, not live measurements in this research. KS01 range conversion, chamfer cut-corner policy, ridge-range boundaries and unequal-radii FP14 parity remain unresolved. No bridge access was used or requested.

A deterministic wonky setback shape policy is still needed before general patches can mean Onshape compatibility. Omitted setback, explicit zero, explicit positive setback and smoothCorners must not be conflated. General G1 constraints alone do not choose a unique corner.

Exact representation policy needs an explicit distinction between elementary analytic, exact algebraic/procedural and certified approximated exchange geometry. The present Curve/Surface variants cannot express KS04's ridge or a general vertex patch; infrastructure ownership is a dependency, not an incidental fillet edit.

The 0.001-mm and 1e-4-rad experimental patch budgets are planning assumptions, not approved project tolerances. Any accepted budgets must compose construction, trimming, exchange and tessellation errors and preserve the 0.05-mm R20 guided-gap allowance; whole-motion clearance was not evaluated.

The existing house-style 'closed-form' volumes sometimes use converged numerical quadrature. Preserve them as valuable independent targets, but obtain analytic integrals or rigorous remainder/interval bounds before advertising certified 1e-12 accuracy. Onshape mean-volume disagreement inside its uncertainty interval is not a reason to weaken geometric checks.

Varady-Rockwood 1997 and Vida-Martin-Varady 1994 full texts remain inaccessible; Zhou-Qian 2010 was only metadata/abstract-level evidence. Full implementation claims for those papers are deliberately withheld. The 2018 Gregory paper and the cited open-source code were actually read.

Licensing/patent clearance is not settled by this research. The inspected transfinite revision is MIT; SISL is AGPL/commercial and OCCT LGPL with exception, for study/oracles only here. Prior notes flag setback patents; do not infer a private-use exemption or current legal status from those notes.
